# Rational Linear Relations and Laplace Equations for Dihedral Modular Graph Functions up to Weight 11

Noah (noah@schittenhelm.dev), Version 2

## Abstract

Two-loop dihedral modular graph functions $C(a,b,c)$ arise in the low-energy expansion of the one-loop closed-string amplitude. We ask how many independent rational linear relations hold among $C(a,b,c)$, $E(w)$ and $\zeta(w)$ at odd weight $w$. A counting of linearly independent modular graph forms exists and predicts higher weights [C-litn4]. We find numerically that the relation space has dimension exactly 1 at weights 3 [C-modular-R1], 5 [C-modular-R1b], 7 [C-modular-R1c], 9 [C-modular-R1d] and 11 [C-modular-R7b]. The weight-9 relation is $960E(9)+\zeta(9)-2160C(4,4,1)-4320C(4,3,2)-960C(3,3,3)=0$ [C-modular-R6a]. - Lattice-sum normalisation of $E(s)$ and $C(a,b,c)$: factors $\big(\tau_2/(\pi|m\tau+n|^2)\big)^a$ [C-modell].
- The weight of $C(a,b,c)$ is $w=a+b+c$, and $\zeta(k)$ is the Riemann zeta value [C-modell].
- Laplacian $L$ is evaluated by a fourth-order finite-difference scheme with step $h=10^{-6}$ [C-modell].
- Verifier points: 4 points, seed 4711, $|\tau_1|\le 1/2$, $1\le\tau_2\le 2.5$ [C-modell].
- Working precision: 32 digits. Tolerance: maximal relative residual $10^{-24}$ ($10^{-14}$ with Laplacian) [C-modell].
- Completeness is tested on normalised value matrices at points with seed 4712 [C-modular-R1].

## Method

**Certificates.** Each modular-graph-function relation is checked by the exact leading Laurent coefficient and numerically at the verifier points to 32 digits [C-modular-R6a]. The dimension of the relation space is read off from a singular-value gap of the normalised value matrix. Singular values below $10^{-24}$ count as kernel and those above $10^{-8}$ as non-kernel [C-modular-R1]. Laplace equations are checked by finite differences at tolerance $10^{-14}$ [C-modell] [C-modular-R4a]. The holomorphic identities and the eta-span table are exact coefficient comparisons with Sturm bounds, resp. an exhaustive exact computation [C-modular-R5a] [C-modular-R8].

**Trusted base and numerical candidates.** The Sturm-bound coefficient comparison is exact. The evaluation of modular graph functions, the finite-difference Laplacian and the singular-value decomposition are floating-point computations [C-modell]. A relation among modular graph functions therefore remains a numerical observation at the verifier points, not a theorem [C-modell] [C-modular-R1].

**Basis origin.** The weight-11 hypothesis basis came from a human-guided exploration and was then verified by the code verifier [C-modular-R7a].

**Execution.** The work was carried out by an automated, verifier-gated laboratory in which a statement is accepted only after code verification (Appendix A) [C-methode].

## Discussion, limitations and open questions

All modular-graph-function statements are numerical observations at 4 verifier points and none is a theorem [C-modell]. Residuals far below the tolerance, the exact leading Laurent coefficient and the singular-value gaps make accidental relations unlikely but do not prove an identity [C-modular-R6a] [C-modular-R1d].

The main limitation concerns the literature. Weights 3 to 7 and the Laplace equations are already stated in the literature or have inconclusive status [C-modular-R1] [C-modular-R1b] [C-modular-R1c] [C-modular-R4a] [C-modular-R4b] [C-modular-R4c] [C-modular-R4d]. At weight 9 the relation may be implied by the counting of [C-litn4] [C-modular-R6e]. At weight 11 the relation was not found in an abstract search, which cannot exclude that explicit coefficients appear in the body of published work [C-modular-R7a] [C-modular-R7b]. We have not compared our relations with explicit formulae in [C-litn3], [C-litn4] or [C-litn9], so we claim no independent relation. The weight-6 case remains undecided [C-neg1].

Open questions:

(i) Do the weight-9 and weight-11 relations follow from the counting of [C-litn4] and the explicit decompositions of [C-litn9] [C-modular-R6e] [C-modular-R7b]?
(ii) Can the weight-9 and weight-11 relations be proved [C-modular-R6e] [C-modular-R7b]?
(iii) What is the relation space at weight 6, with a basis and precision that meet the gap criterion [C-neg1]?
(iv) Is there a feasible route to the full ten-function weight-11 basis [C-neg3]?
